decks.domain: Distractions, collisions, emergencies and adverse weather

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: No preparation can eliminate every driving hazard, but recognizing hazards helps a _____ respond.
cards.back: No preparation can eliminate every driving hazard, but recognizing hazards helps a driver respond.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Before departure, check the travel path, adjust the _____ and mirrors, buckle occupants and remove distractions.
cards.back: Before departure, check the travel path, adjust the seat and mirrors, buckle occupants and remove distractions.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Visual _____ diverts the eyes, manual distraction occupies the hands and cognitive distraction diverts attention.
cards.back: Visual distraction diverts the eyes, manual distraction occupies the hands and cognitive distraction diverts attention.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Texting combines visual, manual and cognitive _____ .
cards.back: Texting combines visual, manual and cognitive distraction.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Eating, grooming, passenger conversation, navigation use and entertainment controls can distract a _____ .
cards.back: Eating, grooming, passenger conversation, navigation use and entertainment controls can distract a driver.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A hands-free device can still cause cognitive _____ even while both hands remain available.
cards.back: A hands-free device can still cause cognitive distraction even while both hands remain available.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Silence or turn off the phone _____ driving to reduce the temptation to respond.
cards.back: Silence or turn off the phone before driving to reduce the temptation to respond.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Pull into a _____ location before making a necessary call or ask a passenger to make it.
cards.back: Pull into a safe location before making a necessary call or ask a passenger to make it.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Study unfamiliar routes _____ setting out rather than reading directions while driving.
cards.back: Study unfamiliar routes before setting out rather than reading directions while driving.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ pets before departure and stop safely before attending to a child’s needs.
cards.back: Secure pets before departure and stop safely before attending to a child’s needs.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Do _____ reach for an item that falls inside the vehicle while driving.
cards.back: Do not reach for an item that falls inside the vehicle while driving.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide groups _____ contributors into equipment problems, roadway design, road maintenance and driver behavior.
cards.back: The guide groups collision contributors into equipment problems, roadway design, road maintenance and driver behavior.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ tires, braking or steering faults can contribute to a collision.
cards.back: Unsafe tires, braking or steering faults can contribute to a collision.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Road debris, _____ and construction can create collision hazards.
cards.back: Road debris, potholes and construction can create collision hazards.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Tailgating, _____ lane changes, speeding and failing to yield are hazardous driver behaviors.
cards.back: Tailgating, unsafe lane changes, speeding and failing to yield are hazardous driver behaviors.

decks.domain: Distractions, collisions, emergencies and adverse weather

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Store loose objects in the trunk when possible so they are less likely to strike occupants in a _____ .
cards.back: Store loose objects in the trunk when possible so they are less likely to strike occupants in a collision.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide recommends keeping writing materials, insurance details and emergency supplies in a _____ kit.
cards.back: The guide recommends keeping writing materials, insurance details and emergency supplies in a collision kit.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Know which braking system the _____ has; the owner’s manual can identify anti-lock equipment.
cards.back: Know which braking system the vehicle has; the owner’s manual can identify anti-lock equipment.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Anti-lock braking helps preserve _____ control by managing wheel lockup.
cards.back: Anti-lock braking helps preserve steering control by managing wheel lockup.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A persistent ABS warning lamp indicates that the system _____ attention.
cards.back: A persistent ABS warning lamp indicates that the system needs attention.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: If an approaching vehicle enters the _____ ’s lane, avoid escaping into the opposing lane.
cards.back: If an approaching vehicle enters the driver’s lane, avoid escaping into the opposing lane.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Wear the lap-and-shoulder belt before every trip as protection if a _____ cannot be avoided.
cards.back: Wear the lap-and-shoulder belt before every trip as protection if a collision cannot be avoided.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A sideways-sliding _____ can roll when a curb, soft ground or another obstruction trips it.
cards.back: A sideways-sliding vehicle can roll when a curb, soft ground or another obstruction trips it.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A higher center of gravity makes a vehicle _____ prone to tipping.
cards.back: A higher center of gravity makes a vehicle more prone to tipping.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Excess speed and abrupt _____ can contribute to a rollover.
cards.back: Excess speed and abrupt steering can contribute to a rollover.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: If the vehicle leaves the pavement, slow gradually rather than jerking the _____ wheel back toward the road.
cards.back: If the vehicle leaves the pavement, slow gradually rather than jerking the steering wheel back toward the road.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Belts help prevent occupants from being ejected during a _____ .
cards.back: Belts help prevent occupants from being ejected during a rollover.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Some side airbags use rollover sensors to help _____ occupants during a rollover.
cards.back: Some side airbags use rollover sensors to help protect occupants during a rollover.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Abrupt turning or stopping on a slippery surface can cause a _____ .
cards.back: Abrupt turning or stopping on a slippery surface can cause a skid.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: In the guide’s rear-skid example, turn toward the _____ in which the rear is sliding without oversteering.
cards.back: In the guide’s rear-skid example, turn toward the direction in which the rear is sliding without oversteering.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Braking and _____ responses can vary with the vehicle’s drive and control systems.
cards.back: Braking and steering responses can vary with the vehicle’s drive and control systems.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Avoid abrupt _____ during traction loss and look toward the desired travel path.
cards.back: Avoid abrupt steering during traction loss and look toward the desired travel path.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Electronic stability control compares the intended _____ with actual vehicle travel and can apply individual brakes to help maintain stability.
cards.back: Electronic stability control compares the intended direction with actual vehicle travel and can apply individual brakes to help maintain stability.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: When hydroplaning, avoid a sudden turn or sudden braking and _____ the accelerator.
cards.back: When hydroplaning, avoid a sudden turn or sudden braking and ease off the accelerator.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: If trapped on _____ with a train approaching, get all occupants out and away from the rail path.
cards.back: If trapped on tracks with a train approaching, get all occupants out and away from the rail path.

decks.domain: Distractions, collisions, emergencies and adverse weather

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: During a tire blowout, hold the wheel firmly and avoid slamming on the _____ .
cards.back: During a tire blowout, hold the wheel firmly and avoid slamming on the brakes.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: After a blowout, keep the vehicle controlled as it slows, then brake gently and stop in a _____ place.
cards.back: After a blowout, keep the vehicle controlled as it slows, then brake gently and stop in a safe place.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: If the accelerator sticks, keep watching the road and shift into _____ .
cards.back: If the accelerator sticks, keep watching the road and shift into neutral.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Do not engage a _____ -lock mechanism while trying to stop a vehicle with a stuck accelerator.
cards.back: Do not engage a steering-lock mechanism while trying to stop a vehicle with a stuck accelerator.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: If the service _____ fail, avoid suddenly applying the parking brake because this can cause loss of control.
cards.back: If the service brakes fail, avoid suddenly applying the parking brake because this can cause loss of control.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A vehicle without working brakes must _____ be driven further; call for assistance.
cards.back: A vehicle without working brakes must not be driven further; call for assistance.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Steam from under the hood can indicate overheating; _____ safely and switch off the engine.
cards.back: Steam from under the hood can indicate overheating; stop safely and switch off the engine.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Do _____ open a hot radiator cap; allow the engine to cool.
cards.back: Do not open a hot radiator cap; allow the engine to cool.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: If smoke comes from under the hood, leave traffic, stop, shut off the engine and get occupants _____ from the vehicle.
cards.back: If smoke comes from under the hood, leave traffic, stop, shut off the engine and get occupants away from the vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Do _____ attempt to fight a large vehicle fire; obtain assistance.
cards.back: Do not attempt to fight a large vehicle fire; obtain assistance.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A vehicle battery can release explosive fumes, so do _____ smoke or use a flame nearby.
cards.back: A vehicle battery can release explosive fumes, so do not smoke or use a flame nearby.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: At the first sign of a breakdown, ease off the accelerator and move smoothly toward a _____ roadside location.
cards.back: At the first sign of a breakdown, ease off the accelerator and move smoothly toward a safe roadside location.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Signal intentions and check traffic carefully when moving a _____ vehicle out of its lane.
cards.back: Signal intentions and check traffic carefully when moving a failing vehicle out of its lane.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Once safely stopped, make the vehicle visible with hazard lamps or _____ warning equipment.
cards.back: Once safely stopped, make the vehicle visible with hazard lamps or reflective warning equipment.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Do not stand immediately _____ or alongside a broken-down vehicle exposed to traffic.
cards.back: Do not stand immediately behind or alongside a broken-down vehicle exposed to traffic.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: If the disabled vehicle remains in the traffic lane, _____ away from it while help is sought.
cards.back: If the disabled vehicle remains in the traffic lane, wait away from it while help is sought.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: When the _____ is safely clear of traffic, the guide recommends waiting inside with doors locked and calling for help.
cards.back: When the vehicle is safely clear of traffic, the guide recommends waiting inside with doors locked and calling for help.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Do _____ try to wave passing vehicles down for assistance.
cards.back: Do not try to wave passing vehicles down for assistance.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: _____ from vehicle exhaust has no smell and can affect occupants without an obvious odor warning.
cards.back: Carbon monoxide from vehicle exhaust has no smell and can affect occupants without an obvious odor warning.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: A leaking exhaust or an engine running in a confined garage can permit _____ to accumulate.
cards.back: A leaking exhaust or an engine running in a confined garage can permit carbon monoxide to accumulate.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide directs a person suspecting exhaust-gas poisoning to get _____ immediately.
cards.back: The guide directs a person suspecting exhaust-gas poisoning to get fresh air immediately.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Do _____ attempt to drive through a flooded roadway; turn back and select another route.
cards.back: Do not attempt to drive through a flooded roadway; turn back and select another route.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Floodwater can _____ a damaged or washed-out road even when the water looks shallow.
cards.back: Floodwater can hide a damaged or washed-out road even when the water looks shallow.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: If no alternate route is available, _____ on higher ground for floodwater to recede.
cards.back: If no alternate route is available, wait on higher ground for floodwater to recede.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: If a vehicle enters _____ , the guide directs occupants to begin escaping immediately instead of waiting inside.
cards.back: If a vehicle enters water, the guide directs occupants to begin escaping immediately instead of waiting inside.

decks.domain: Distractions, collisions, emergencies and adverse weather

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: The guide’s _____ -escape cue POGO means releasing belts, opening windows and getting out.
cards.back: The guide’s water-escape cue POGO means releasing belts, opening windows and getting out.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: After a collision involving injury, death or damage, stop when _____ and identify yourself rather than leaving the scene.
cards.back: After a collision involving injury, death or damage, stop when safe and identify yourself rather than leaving the scene.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Request _____ assistance after a collision and an ambulance when needed.
cards.back: Request police assistance after a collision and an ambulance when needed.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Collect involved persons’ names and witness details _____ a crash.
cards.back: Collect involved persons’ names and witness details after a crash.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Drivers _____ exchange their name, address and vehicle identification details and show a license when requested.
cards.back: Drivers must exchange their name, address and vehicle identification details and show a license when requested.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: If an unattended vehicle or property is damaged, notify _____ , seek the owner and leave identifying contact information.
cards.back: If an unattended vehicle or property is damaged, notify police, seek the owner and leave identifying contact information.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Document travel _____ , lane, occupants, date, time and weather after a crash.
cards.back: Document travel direction, lane, occupants, date, time and weather after a crash.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Notify the _____ as soon as practical after a collision.
cards.back: Notify the insurer as soon as practical after a collision.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Do _____ move an injured person unless an immediate life-threatening danger requires it.
cards.back: Do not move an injured person unless an immediate life-threatening danger requires it.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: Before leaving a vehicle unattended, stop the engine, _____ the ignition, remove the key and apply the brake.
cards.back: Before leaving a vehicle unattended, stop the engine, secure the ignition, remove the key and apply the brake.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: For an approaching authorized emergency vehicle using warning signals, yield, move toward the _____ edge and stop until it passes.
cards.back: For an approaching authorized emergency vehicle using warning signals, yield, move toward the right edge and stop until it passes.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: On a multilane road near a stopped emergency _____ , change into a nonadjacent lane only when that can be done safely.
cards.back: On a multilane road near a stopped emergency vehicle, change into a nonadjacent lane only when that can be done safely.

cards.front: Complete the guide’s rule: If moving over is _____ or impossible, slow to a reasonably safe speed for the conditions.
cards.back: If moving over is unsafe or impossible, slow to a reasonably safe speed for the conditions.
